items.proposed_content: Proposition 3.1 makes phase-space measure an unreliable proxy for spectral relevance: under a two-dimensional fixed set for a common geodesic-flow period and additional technical assumptions, a periodic family can force lower bounds on an averaged counting remainder and number variance even though the family has measure zero. This conclusion is hypothesis-sensitive; the stated proposition is for compact boundaryless surfaces, while its application to stadium bouncing-ball trajectories is presented by analogy, and the span does not supply the later proof mechanism.
Amplification trades spectral averaging for targeted coherence: coefficients are chosen so the desired eigenstate adds constructively while the geometric cost remains countable.
An integral transform compresses a spatial correlation into one L-value. Convexity is exactly the barrier at which the error ceases to decay, so subconvexity has a direct geometric interpretation.

The unit establishes an evidential dependency rather than a theorem: finite computation supports a conjecture that the even modular spectrum is simple, and the source explicitly flags that conjecture as an input with later applications. The gain is a clearly named hypothesis motivated by data; the loss is global certainty, since checking finitely many eigenvalues neither proves simplicity nor explains how the cited later theorem uses it.
Classical chaotic dynamics does not determine spectral statistics once arithmetic symmetries introduce additional correlations. Different observables can retain or lose universality independently.

Invariant-torus quantization and the stable-closed-geodesic construction provide two source-supported routes from classical invariant sets to concentrating quasimodes: the former uses action variables, while the latter yields a sparse eigenvalue progression and quasimodes converging toward arc-length measure on the geodesic. Negative curvature does not supply either stable construction; it presents unstable periodic orbits whose spectral influence the source explicitly leaves unresolved, so failure of the integrable route is not evidence that unstable localization cannot occur.
Arithmetic degeneracy prevents the cancellation expected from generic chaotic orbit lengths. Bounded clustering is the intermediate structural property that makes this coherence estimable.

The local bound ignores global geometry; Hecke weights inject global arithmetic coherence. Framing the conjecture beside Lindelöf separates a generic convexity-scale barrier from the deeper cancellation needed to beat it.

The quotient representation places chaotic constant-negative-curvature dynamics and spectral type in one framework, while compactness marks a decisive boundary. A compact quotient supports a discrete eigenstate study; for the noncompact modular quotient, bound states are not automatic and cusp-form eigenvalues coexist with continuous Eisenstein spectrum. Thus the representation gains a common geometric language but does not justify treating all hyperbolic quotients, or all their states, as spectrally alike.

A trace singularity is a frequency-domain witness of coherent periodic dynamics. The calculus lemma prevents smoothing from hiding the minimum amount of real counting fluctuation required to generate that witness.

The lower-bound construction reverses amplification: instead of selecting a known state, it engineers a location and correspondence product where collective arithmetic fixedness must be expressed by some large states.

The same hidden structure can be both obstruction and instrument. It breaks generic universality predictions for some observables while creating nonlocal operators that make otherwise inaccessible individual questions tractable.
The change of parameter preserves the classical-quantum correspondence question while exposing concrete spectral objects: eigenvalues, eigenfunctions, and their high-energy limits.
Nonlocal symmetry tests a localized measure by cloning information across separated regions. Isolation of one branch prevents cancellation or redistribution among several singular images.

Commutation preserves energy while nonlocality moves spatial information. This combination supplies extra labels and identities inside an eigenspace without changing the underlying quantum Hamiltonian.
A specially symmetric point acts as an arithmetic decoder: geometric orbit summation becomes an L-value whose growth can be read from a sup-norm estimate.

A density-one theorem is an aggregate statement, not individual control. Invariance is a necessary structural constraint shared by Liouville measure and singular orbit measures, so it cannot alone rule out scarring.
A distributional statistic tests random-wave behavior more sharply than visual inspection: it asks whether local amplitudes collectively have the predicted law.
A failed model need not be discarded wholesale; the correct move is to identify which operator's spectrum carries the symmetry class the model describes.

Convexity is the baseline forced by two-sided analytic control, whereas stronger cancellation depends on Euler-product arithmetic. Organizing bounds by t, conductor, and spectral parameters exposes which complexity variable is being controlled.

A sparsity constraint at one evaluation functional redistributes mass onto the nonvanishing states. Arithmetic lifting therefore creates a structured exceptional family invisible to a generic random-wave model.

Unfolding forgets global spectral density while preserving local spacing structure. Number variance compresses many-level correlations into a rigidity statistic that distinguishes independent from repelling spectra.
Deformation tests whether a bound state is structurally protected. A nonzero coupling to the continuum destroys it, while multiplicity determines whether that mechanism can be applied state by state.

Special-value identities replace a spatial amplitude question by central-value growth. The normalization estimate accounts for the information that must be preserved for the translation to be reversible at the conjectural scale.
